raw_response:
I am 40 years old and have been farming my 4.1 mu in Quzhou for 15 years. My family has four mouths to feed, and my wife and I also do some off-farm work when we can, so I cannot waste time or money on things that do not work. I learned farming from my father and from watching my neighbors. I only went to primary school, but I know my land.

This year, I will do what has worked for me before. For **winter wheat**, I will rotary-till the whole 4.1 mu before sowing in October. I will sow *shinong082*, an improved variety that my neighbors also grow. I do not buy hybrid wheat seeds — improved varieties are good enough and the seed is cheaper. For fertilizer, I will spread a bag of general compound fertilizer at sowing, and then top-dress with another bag of special compound fertilizer in spring. I have a well, so I can irrigate when needed. I will water four times: once before winter, once at green-up, once at jointing, and once during grain filling. That is what my father did, and it gives me about 950 jin per mu. For pests, I will spray insecticide twice and herbicide once. I do not usually bother with fungicide on wheat unless the weather is very wet.

For **summer maize**, as soon as the wheat is harvested in early June, I will plant *denghai662* hybrid seeds directly into the stubble without tilling. No-till saves me time and fuel, and the maize grows fine if I plant quickly after the wheat comes off. I will put down one bag of compound fertilizer when I sow. I will irrigate twice — once if it is dry after sowing, and again at the big trumpet stage. I will spray insecticide once and herbicide once. I expect around 900 jin per mu of maize.

My family needs both crops. The wheat gives us flour for the year, and the maize sells for cash and feeds our animals. I keep my inputs simple because I know my land, and I do not have money to waste.
